summary: See how many are in a small group, up to 5, at a glance without counting.
Say the counting numbers in order from 1 to 31 and know the written numbers in that order.
Count objects in a row by touching each one once while saying one number, to 15 and past it.
Know that the last number said when counting up to 10 things tells how many there are.
Make a group of a given size and count groups, from 1 to 10 and beyond.
Count or match up two groups of up to 10 to tell which has more, which has fewer, or if they are the same.
Read and write some of the numbers from 1 to 10.
Solve everyday putting-together and taking-apart problems with up to 8 things, using objects, fingers or acting out.
Start to build and break apart groups of up to 8 in different ways with objects or fingers.
Spot a simple AB repeating pattern and keep it going.
Copy a simple AB pattern, making it again with different things.
Find the part that repeats in a harder pattern, like ABB or ABC, and keep it going.
Know and name circles, squares, triangles and rectangles whatever their size or turn.
Describe and sort flat and solid shapes by features like size, sides and corners.
Put flat shapes together to make a new shape, like two squares making a rectangle.
Build things in play with solid shapes like blocks, balls and cylinders.
Say where things are compared with each other using words like beside, next to, between, over and under, and show it with models.
Follow directions to move around a space and find a place in it.
Measure things with tools, both everyday objects like blocks and real ones like a ruler.
Name what can be measured, like length and weight, and compare two things side by side to solve a problem.
Put up to 6 things in order by height or length.
Show information in charts, graphs and tally marks, and talk about what it shows.
Begin to guess what a count or survey will show before collecting it.
